title: Objective Decoupling in Social Reinforcement Learning: Recovering Ground Truth from Sycophantic Majorities

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating agent behavior in a Gridworld environment where a majority of evaluators provide false high rewards for a neutral proxy ('Candy') while downplaying safety hazards ('Lava'), measuring the agent's ability to recover the latent ground truth using sparse safety axioms.

Testing continuous control in a Hopper-v4 environment where a majority of evaluators penalize effort (movement/velocity) to simulate laziness, measuring if the agent can filter the feedback to recover the true high-velocity hopping policy.
Simulating strategic adversaries and bias contagion in a K-armed Social Bandit setting to measure the agent's ability to dynamically isolate corrupted feedback sources and minimize latent regret.
